name: NJ-12
label: Safe D

key_factors: Huge Democratic fundraising and outside-spending advantage
Republican candidate nearly unfunded with no outside support
Open seat removes incumbency factor but not the partisan baseline
model.rationale: The district's D+13 lean plus a favorable environment points to a roughly 20-point Democratic margin, and Polymarket prices the Democratic nominee at 97%. Hamawy's $1.5 million raised and $1.9 million in outside support against Mele's $79,000 reinforce the lopsided resource picture.
model.watch: A late surge of outside Republican spending or an unusually strong national GOP environment could narrow the margin, though not enough to threaten the seat.
notes: No expert rater lists this race; treated as safe for the party holding the seat.
No usable general-election polls; forecast rests on fundamentals and expert ratings.
Open seat: Bonnie Watson Coleman (D) is not on the ballot.

overview:
Bonnie Watson Coleman's retirement leaves this central New Jersey seat open, but the district's D+13 partisan lean keeps it firmly in Democratic hands on paper. The fundamentals point to a margin in the low twenties before any candidate-specific adjustments.

The money gap is stark: Democrat Adam Hamawy has raised about $1.5 million with nearly $2 million in outside support, while Republican Gregg Mele has raised under $80,000 and drawn no outside spending. Prediction markets price the Democratic nominee around 97%, consistent with a Safe D rating. With no public polling available, the forecast rests on fundamentals, but every available signal points the same way.
